scenarios.behaviour: A logged-in user with an empty bag sees 'Your shopping bag is empty' on the cart page.
Each line in the bag shows the product's name and unit price.
Each line's total is its unit price times its quantity.
The bag's summary shows the total quantity across all of its lines.
The bag's summary total is the sum of every line's total.
A line shows the product's current catalog price, even when the price changed after the product was added.
scenarios.sourceNote: src/WebApp/Services/BasketState.cs:138-144: the bag stores only product ids and quantities; name and price are read from the catalog each time the bag is shown

scenarios.behaviour: The bag keeps its items after the user logs out and logs in again.
scenarios.sourceNote: src/Basket.API/Repositories/RedisBasketRepository.cs:37: the bag is stored in Redis under the user's id, with no expiry

scenarios.behaviour: Pages still load for a user whose bag holds a product that was later deleted from the catalog.
scenarios.sourceNote: Suspected eShop bug. src/WebApp/Services/BasketState.cs:138 indexes catalogItems[item.ProductId] for every bag line, so a deleted product has no entry. Seen live 2026-11-27 with a test-owned user and catalog item: after deleting the bagged item through the Catalog API, both / and /cart return 200 and never render for that user (nothing readable after 30 s). The header's CartMenu reads the bag on every page.

scenarios.behaviour: Adding a product from its item page puts it in the bag with quantity 1.
Adding a product that is already in the bag raises that line's quantity by 1 instead of adding a second line.
An item page says how many of that product are in the bag: '<N> in your shopping bag'.
The increase button raises a line's quantity by 1.
The decrease button lowers a line's quantity by 1.
Typing a quantity and pressing Enter sets the line to that quantity.
Remove takes the line out of the bag.
Removing the bag's last line shows the empty bag.
The decrease button is disabled while a line's quantity is 1.
A typed quantity below 1, or one that isn't a number, becomes 1.
scenarios.sourceNote: src/WebApp/wwwroot/js/cart-quantity.js:24. The Basket API also rejects quantities below 1 in its model (src/Basket.API/Model/BasketItem.cs:13), but UpdateBasket never runs that validation; the API is gRPC, which the inventory doesn't list, so no row can owe an API test for it.

scenarios.behaviour: When the bag isn't empty, the header's bag link is named 'Shopping bag, <N> items' with the bag's total quantity, or 'Shopping bag, 1 item' for one.
scenarios.sourceNote: src/WebApp/Components/Layout/CartMenu.razor:31. The header shows on every page; listed under /cart.

scenarios.behaviour: The header's bag badge shows '99+' when the bag holds more than 99 items.
Opening the cart while logged out leads to the login page.
scenarios.sourceNote: src/WebApp/Components/Pages/Cart/CartPage.razor:6 ([Authorize]). Seen live 2026-11-25 by the cart-mapping agent: redirect to Identity's login on port 5243.

scenarios.behaviour: A logged-out user's item page offers 'Log in to purchase' instead of 'Add to shopping bag', and it leads to the login page.
A user's bag holds only what that user added; another user's bag is separate.
scenarios.sourceNote: src/Basket.API/Grpc/BasketService.cs:15, :38, :61: every call reads and writes the bag of the caller's own user id

scenarios.behaviour: The empty bag's 'Start shopping' link goes to the catalog.
'Check out' in the bag's summary goes to the checkout page.
'Continue shopping' in the bag's summary goes back to the catalog.
After the user places an order, their bag is empty.
scenarios.sourceNote: src/WebApp/Services/BasketState.cs:108 (checkout deletes the bag); src/Basket.API/IntegrationEvents/EventHandling/OrderStartedIntegrationEventHandler.cs:14; eShop's own test OrderStartedEventRemovesUsersBasket (tests/Basket.UnitTests/BasketServiceTests.cs:130)
